messages:
Maya: Quick sync — we've got two competing asks for the catalog sprint: fast-entry for small customers vs. stable rollouts for enterprise. Which do we prioritize?
Carlos: Depends on SLA triggers. Enterprise wants pinned model guarantees.
Jun: Ops note: fast-entry increases churn on infra configs, more canary noise :grimacing:
Priya: From PM side, revenue signal favors fast-entry for SMB growth. Enterprise renewals push for stability.
Maya: Can we propose a hybrid lane? "fast-entry" for cohort A (<=10k tokens/mo) and "stable-rollout" for cohort B with pin & 30d deprecation notice.
Carlos: +1. Needs automation: pinning API + rolloff warnings. I can scope infra work (2 sprints?)
Jun: For canaries, suggest these acceptance checks:

```
- latency P95 <= 350ms
- token-cost delta <= +15%
- quality regression < 1% on eval suite
```

If any fail, auto-fallback to previous stable model.
Priya: Who owns the eval suite? Product or Research?
Maya: Research will maintain evals; product defines pass thresholds. We'll add a docs page for pin exceptions.
oncall-bot: Deploy notice: canary rollout started for tenant-group 'alpha-small' — 12 hosts
Carlos: Thumbs up from infra, but we need a rollback playbook. Drafting in #eng-runtime
Maya: Action items:
- Priya: write adoption criteria & SLA mapping (owner)
- Carlos: pin API + rollback playbook (owner)
- Jun: canary acceptance automation (owner)
- Research: finalize eval suites for cohorts

Let's reconvene Wed 11am. @everyone please add objections in thread.

Priya: Noted. Also, customer ask: allow 14-day opt-in for pin exceptions. We should list that in the comms.
Maya: Good call. Add to playbook. :white_check_mark:
Carlos: Estimating infra impact: ~3% cluster overhead for pinned replicas, might need dedicated capacity flag in catalog metadata.
Jun: We'll need metrics on churn & canary failures to evaluate after 2 sprints.
Maya: Thanks all — will capture in roadmap doc after Wed.
